text:
anya: Quick question — are we still leaning gRPC + protobuf for the internal control plane? thinking about gateways + console UX.
sam: Yes from perf side. unary/streaming and smaller wire size matters for kv/cache calls. also easier to enforce schemas.
maria: +1 on schemas but browsers and 3rd party integ worry me. grpc-web + Envoy works but adds ops surface. @leo any take on gateway cost?
leo: Gateway adds ~1 hop but we can do a thin HTTP front that transcodes to proto for internal services. keep public REST shapes for the console.
product_jamie: Console teams asked for human-friendly error shapes and consistent status codes. grpc errors->http mapping has been messy in past rollouts.
sam: We can standardize mapping: always return JSON {code,message,details} and map gRPC status to http 4xx/5xx at the gateway. keeps clients simple.
anya: Can we share a minimal envoy route that does grpc_web + cors? would help unblock console.
leo: snippet:
```
- match: { prefix: '/internal.api.v1' }
  route: { cluster: 'control-plane' }
  grpc_web: true
  cors: true
```
maria: Also we need quota propagation header (x-rw-route-key). If gateway terminates TLS we must forward original auth and quota headers.
deploy-bot: CI pipeline note: proto changes must bump service-major in registry and trigger canary push to 5% traffic before full rollout :robot_face: 
product_jamie: UX: canary needs console flag to toggle new endpoints; ops should be able to flip without code deploy.
sam: That argues for a stable gateway surface we control — internal services can change proto but gateway keeps backward-compatible HTTP facade.
anya: Sounds like plan: grpc+proto inside, gateway HTTP facade for console/3rd-party, strict schema registry + canary. I'll write an RFC draft.
maria: Please include telemetry: per-route token breakdown, client version in traces, and quota deltas. small examples of logs would help.
anya: Will do. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
